competitors.name: Aldi / Mama Cozzi's / Richelieu Foods
competitors.action: A nationwide health alert hit two Mama Cozzi's frozen breakfast pizzas sold at Aldi after recalled dry milk powder in the cheese raised possible Salmonella risk, a sharp reminder that private-label frozen pizza programs can take fast brand damage from upstream ingredient failures.

competitors.name: Dr. Oetker / Ristorante
competitors.action: Dr. Oetker reintroduced its Ristorante Pollo pizza for convenience retailers starting in May, which is a useful signal that established frozen pizza brands are still tuning channel-specific assortments instead of relying on one broad grocery-only range.

trends.topic: Frozen pizza competition is splitting between sharper channel targeting and higher supply-chain risk
trends.magnitude: Dr. Oetker is tailoring a convenience-specific reintroduction while Aldi's private-label breakfast pizzas were pulled into a nationwide health alert tied to an upstream dairy ingredient recall.
trends.context: The useful read for Real Dough is that distribution wins still matter, but execution discipline matters just as much. A clean, credible premium story can get undercut quickly if manufacturing or ingredient control slips.

market_data.value: 2 breakfast pizzas with best-by dates of Oct. 15 and Oct. 21-24, 2026

breaking.headline: The cleanest signal today is that frozen pizza upside and downside are both getting more channel-specific
breaking.impact: One brand is using convenience-only assortment tuning to stay relevant, while another got dragged into a national safety issue through a private-label supply chain. Real Dough should keep building tight retail stories, but it also needs obsessive supplier and QA discipline if it wants premium trust to hold.
